headline: Watch, steady: the Iran standoff is unchanged overnight and last night's GPS-jamming flags have eased; nothing urgent for SA.
summary: No new strikes on Iran were confirmed overnight, and the GPS-jamming flags over the Gulf and Israel have eased back to normal. Hormuz still carries only about 4 ships a day and the Australian dollar fell to 67.8 US cents, so SA fuel stays expensive. Microsoft says this week's Microsoft 365 outage was not a cyber attack. Locally: Moderate fire danger in the Hills, no bans or warnings, grid and phone networks normal.
actions: Keep the car tank and any generator fuel at least half full while Hormuz stays closed.
Check your bushfire plan and CFS app watch zones this weekend as Fire Danger Seasons start across SA.

categories.summary: No new strikes on Iran confirmed since the reported hit on Sirik on 12 November; Trump's warnings and the new US task force against Iran's land supply routes keep tension high. Overnight GPS-jamming flags over the Gulf and Israel have eased to normal. Taiwan, Korea and Russia-NATO show no warning signs; forecast markets are flat.

sources.title: Fox News: Tehran weighs nuclear treaty exit

categories.summary: US nuclear-command and tanker aircraft are normal and there is no private-jet movement to retreat destinations. Iran's talk of leaving the nuclear treaty raises long-run risk but there is no sign of any nuclear alert.

categories.name: Cyber & infrastructure

sources.title: AAP: Grim Outlook for Teams as Microsoft hit by outage
ABC: 'No indication' Outlook outage caused by cyber attack, Microsoft says

categories.summary: Microsoft says the global Microsoft 365 outage that hit Australian hospitals and agencies was not a cyber attack. Phone carriers and the SA grid are normal, the global threat level is green and exploited-flaw counts are slightly above usual. An overnight 'banking & payments outage' flag was a false match; the ACSC feed timed out this run.

categories.name: Pandemic & biological
categories.summary: The Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak continues in DR Congo, Kenya and Nigeria (reports say Congo cases have passed 10,000) with no cases outside Africa. The lit 'chemical attack' sign is a historical Syria story. Adelaide emergency departments are normal.

categories.name: Natural hazards
categories.summary: Fire danger Moderate in the Mount Lofty Ranges today and tomorrow and no rating for Adelaide; no fire bans, CFS warnings or severe-weather warnings. A strong wind warning is out for Spencer Gulf on Sunday. Two small fires active across SA; several outback roads in the north-east remain closed by flooding.

categories.name: Fuel, food & supply
categories.summary: Hormuz traffic is still only about 4 ships a day (versus 100+ before the war). Brent is about US$95.70 and the Australian dollar fell to 67.8 US cents, so SA fuel prices stay high. Malacca, Lombok, Sunda and Torres routes into Australia are normal.

categories.name: Markets & finance
categories.summary: Brent US$95.74 (flat), VIX 19.7 (+5%), gold US$3,893 (+0.2%), AUD 0.678 (-1.0%). Markets calm overall; a weaker dollar and firm oil are the main cost pressures for SA households.

actions.action: Keep the car and any generator fuel at least half full.
actions.reason: In an escalation, stations run dry within days from panic buying; a half tank covers about a week of essential trips.

actions.action: Hold a little cash at home.
actions.reason: If fuel is rationed or networks fail, cash still works when cards may not.

drivers: No new strikes on Iran have been confirmed since the reported hit on Sirik on 12 November; Trump's warnings and the new US 'Task Force Iron Gate' against Iran's land supply routes keep tension high.
Overnight GPS-jamming flags over the Persian Gulf (40%) and Israel (19%) have eased back to normal levels and were not linked to any confirmed attack.
Hormuz still carries about 4 ships a day (100+ before the war); forecast markets give about 22% for a Hormuz deal by year end.
